===== _claude/shared/instructions/projects-and-sync.md =====
# Projects, Claude files and shared data (axhub-projects@1)

## Where things are
| What | In a project | On the hub (`/projects`, its own Docker volume) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest | `project.manifest.json` (project-manifest@1) | `/projects/<name>/_data/project.manifest.json` |
| Claude files | `_claude/` (rules/, instructions/, memory/) | `/projects/<name>/_claude/` |
| Shared Claude files (every project) | `_claude/shared/` (same sections) | `/projects/_shared/_claude/` |
| Shared data | the manifest's `data.shared` paths, where they are in the project | `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>` |
| Outside any project | `~/.config/claude-sync/shared/` | `/projects/_shared/_claude/` |

`<name>` is the manifest's `name`. A repo can hold several projects: every folder with a manifest is one
(AmberX-AXF holds `amberx-axf` at its root plus `axf-demo`, `axf-console-web` and `axf-console-android` in `apps/`).
Layout schema: `clients/claude-code/projects.schema.json` in the axHub repo. Manifest schema and rules:
`framework/schemas/project-manifest.json` and `framework/schemas/project-rules.json` in AmberX-AXF.

## Session start
A SessionStart hook runs `claude-sync start`. It never creates a manifest (only projects built with or for AmberX,
plus axHub, belong on the hub; add one with `axf project init`, or make any folder a Claude project with
`claude-project` / `/claude-project`, which also creates its GitHub or VPS repo). It creates `_claude/` in every folder that has a
manifest and lacks it, syncs all of them, then prints the rules,
instructions and memory (shared first) and lists anything in a `docs/` folder. Held files are listed at the top:
ask Brett which copy to keep.

## Saving
Edit the files directly, then run `claude-sync sync`, then commit. On claude.ai, with no shell: axHub `call` →
`axhub.memory_write` with `project` = manifest name or `shared`, `area` = `claude` (default) or `data`, and
`path` inside it.

## Commands
- `claude-sync status` / `claude-sync projects`: where it syncs, the projects found, data paths, held files.
- `claude-sync sync`: sync every project in this repo now.
- `claude-sync resolve <id> --keep local|hub` (or `--all`), in that project's folder: settle a held file. Deleting on the hub asks for his approval in axHub first.
- `claude-sync init [dir]`: add a draft manifest and `_claude/` to an AmberX project.
- Setup per device: `node ~/axHub/clients/claude-code/claude-sync.mjs install`, then `claude-sync login` (the axHub token) where `/projects` isn't mounted (the VPS shell, laptops, the phone).
- Validate a manifest: `node framework/cli/project.mjs validate [dir]` in AmberX-AXF, or Dev Console → Standards.

===== _claude/shared/instructions/projects-and-sync.md =====
# Projects, Claude files and shared data (axhub-projects@1)

## Where things are
| What | In a project | On the hub (`/projects`, its own Docker volume) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest | `project.manifest.json` (project-manifest@1) | `/projects/<name>/_data/project.manifest.json` |
| Claude files | `_claude/` (rules/, instructions/, memory/) | `/projects/<name>/_claude/` |
| Shared Claude files (every project) | `_claude/shared/` (same sections) | `/projects/_shared/_claude/` |
| Shared data | the manifest's `data.shared` paths, where they are in the project | `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>` |
| Outside any project | `~/.config/claude-sync/shared/` | `/projects/_shared/_claude/` |

`<name>` is the manifest's `name`. A repo can hold several projects: every folder with a manifest is one
(AmberX-AXF holds `amberx-axf` at its root plus `axf-demo`, `axf-console-web` and `axf-console-android` in `apps/`).
Layout schema: `clients/claude-code/projects.schema.json` in the axHub repo. Manifest schema and rules:
`framework/schemas/project-manifest.json` and `framework/schemas/project-rules.json` in AmberX-AXF.

## Session start
A SessionStart hook runs `claude-sync start`. It never creates a manifest (only projects built with or for AmberX,
plus axHub, belong on the hub; add one with `axf project init`, or make any folder a Claude project with
`claude-project` / `/claude-project`, which also creates its GitHub or VPS repo). It creates `_claude/` in every folder that has a
manifest and lacks it, syncs all of them, then prints the rules,
instructions and memory (shared first) and lists anything in a `docs/` folder. Held files are listed at the top:
ask Brett which copy to keep.

## Saving
Edit the files directly, then run `claude-sync sync`, then commit. On claude.ai, with no shell: axHub `call` →
`axhub.memory_write` with `project` = manifest name or `shared`, `area` = `claude` (default) or `data`, and
`path` inside it.

## Commands
- `claude-sync status` / `claude-sync projects`: where it syncs, the projects found, data paths, held files.
- `claude-sync sync`: sync every project in this repo now.
- `claude-sync resolve <id> --keep local|hub` (or `--all`), in that project's folder: settle a held file. Deleting on the hub asks for his approval in axHub first.
- `claude-sync init [dir]`: add a draft manifest and `_claude/` to an AmberX project.
- Setup per device: `node ~/axHub/clients/claude-code/claude-sync.mjs install`, then `claude-sync login` (the axHub token) where `/projects` isn't mounted (the VPS shell, laptops, the phone).
- Validate a manifest: `node framework/cli/project.mjs validate [dir]` in AmberX-AXF, or Dev Console → Standards.

# Threads and builds log

Every Claude session reads this file when it loads the project and keeps it current, so work can be picked up from
any session, account or machine. The repo is the source of truth; chat history is not.

**Read it before doing anything.** Then update it (edit the thread's row, or add one), set *Updated*, commit and push
with your branch, whenever:

- a thread is made, or a session starts something (a build, edit, fix, test run, push, pull or merge);
- a build completes, or anything fails;
- tests start, pass, fail, or stop part way (say where);
- a push or pull is needed, completes or fails;
- a PR is opened, needs merging, is merged, or the merge fails;
- a deploy is needed;
- the session runs out of credits or hits a usage limit (state `stopped`, the step it was on, how to resume);
- it needs Brett (state `blocked`, the exact question), or an item is queued.

Move rows to *Done* once their PR is merged or the work is dropped. Queued items stay queued until Brett says to run
them (project rule). Open PRs: check GitHub, not this file, before acting on one. If a session can't push, it says
so in its reply and puts the row in its change-log entry so the next session can add it.

**Every unfinished thread can be carried on from another account (Oct 26 2026, Brett):** each row that isn't done
has a block under *To carry on* with everything a new session on any Claude account needs and nothing from chat:
what was asked (in full), the model, the branch and what's already on it, what's left as steps, files to read first,
the checks to run, what it's waiting on (the exact question when it needs Brett), and a ready first message. Write
the block when the thread starts and update it at every step, before the session ends or runs out, so a cut-off
session loses nothing.

States: `working`, `testing`, `review` (PR open / needs merge), `deploy` (merged, needs a deploy), `queued` (waiting
for Brett's go), `blocked` (needs Brett), `failed`, `stopped` (cut off: out of credits, usage limit, session ended),
`on hold`, `done`.

Move rows to *Done* once their PR is merged or the work is dropped. Queued items stay queued until Brett says to run
them (project rule). Open PRs: check GitHub, not this file, before acting on one. If a session can't push, it says
so in its reply and puts the row in its change-log entry so the next session can add it.

**Every unfinished thread can be carried on from another account (Oct 26 2026, Brett):** each row that isn't done
has a block under *To carry on* with everything a new session on any Claude account needs and nothing from chat:
what was asked (in full), the model, the branch and what's already on it, what's left as steps, files to read first,
the checks to run, what it's waiting on (the exact question when it needs Brett), and a ready first message. Write
the block when the thread starts and update it at every step, before the session ends or runs out, so a cut-off
session loses nothing.

States: `working`, `testing`, `review` (PR open / needs merge), `deploy` (merged, needs a deploy), `queued` (waiting
for Brett's go), `blocked` (needs Brett), `failed`, `stopped` (cut off: out of credits, usage limit, session ended),
`on hold`, `done`.

project/initialization/axhub-context.md:69:- **Policy engine:** per-service and per-tool `allow` / `confirm` / `deny`. Shell and destructive actions are default-deny. Since step 2: disabled services deny and are never contacted, SSH is denied unless a tool policy says otherwise, destructive tools are never below `confirm`, and evaluation is fail-closed (own-property lookups only, so tool names like `toString` can't slip through). A `confirm` call returns `confirmation_required` + id; **only the user approves it, out-of-band** (the operator CLI, or since decision #82 the approvals page `/auth/admin/approvals` for signed-in admins, phone first), never the AI client that asked. Since decision #101 the hub **keeps the call** (the MCP default) and runs it itself once approved, so Claude sends it once and never polls; the result is on a job the caller reads with `get_job` if it needs it (`hold: false` keeps the old retry-with-the-id flow). Since decision #103 (**veto everywhere**, server default `AXHUB_CONFIRM_AS=veto`) every call that would wait for an approval is held on the veto countdown instead and runs unless Brett denies it; approvals only come back with `AXHUB_CONFIRM_AS=confirm`. Since decision #102 a tool can also be **`veto`** (per tool; `vps.run` and `vps.logs`): the call is held on a countdown (default 180 s) and **Vinnie**, axHub's own agent, runs it by itself when the countdown ends unless the owner taps **Deny** first (no Approve; never more than 60 s late, else it expires); the approval page, the feeds and the console banner show the countdown, Vinnie pushes `held` / `warning` (30 s) / `running` through the ntfy topic the AmberX app delivers, and the job's output streams live at `/auth/api/jobs/<jobId>/stream` (contract `docs/veto.md`, veto@1). An approval shows the complete call (every argument, invisible characters escaped; calls with over 8000 characters of arguments can't be approved), the CLI asks y/N, and only the hub can issue approval requests. It is bound to the caller, the exact tool (including its definition) and arguments, single-use, and expires in 30 minutes. Since decision #95 the approvals page is a grid of every request (pending first; Approve on a collapsed row only when the row shows the complete call) with Approve, Decline, Postpone (a time or a condition from an open registry: time, service healthy, job done, public https URL answers), Ignore, Revoke and Reopen; a postponed request never runs, returns to pending (never approved) when its condition holds — checked every 5 minutes, reminders every 30 —, and can wait at most 7 days from when it was asked. Every change is compare-and-set on status + revision and audited. Since decision #96 these pages (and Users, Account, Apps, Handoff) are the AXHub web app on the hub's own address, calling the hub's session-only JSON API `/auth/api/*` (hub Origin + `X-AxHub-CSRF`, never the bearer token); the hub's old page addresses redirect there. Connectors receive the tool the hub checked, so a downstream that changes a tool can't run something else under its name (REST tools are signed with their exact request).
project/initialization/axhub-planning.md:115:| 103 | **Veto everywhere** (Oct 30 2026, built on Opus; branch `claude/veto-everywhere`; Brett: "It's not an approval system anymore. It's a veto system … you send the notice that you're going to be making changes, and then my VPS waits three minutes … unless I click deny … you don't stop, you just build and you don't check for its completion"). Hub option `confirmAs` (`HubOptions.confirmAs`, server env `AXHUB_CONFIRM_AS`, **default `veto`** on the server; `confirm` brings approvals back; the core default stays `confirm` for embedders and tests): every call that would wait for an approval (`confirm`, from any rule: service default, tool policy, destructive raise, MCP services) is held on the veto countdown instead (the tool's `vetoSettings`, else 180/30 s) and Vinnie runs it unless denied. `allow` and `deny` unchanged; disabled services and SSH without a tool policy still deny; a reason is still required. `describe_service` shows `veto`. Sessions send the call once with its reason, tell Brett it's coming, and carry on: no waiting, no checking, no `get_job` unless the result is needed. 450 tests. |
  countdown stops it). The AI client can never approve, hurry or un-deny one: there is no approve action for a veto
  hold, and re-sending with the `confirmation_id` only answers "counting down". The caller cancelling its own held job
  (`cancel_job`) is a Deny.
- `vps.run` and `vps.logs` are `veto` in `deploy/ssh-shell.sh`; the live hub's migration is in `examples/README.md`.

### Veto everywhere (decision #103)

The server holds **every** call that would need an approval on the veto countdown (`AXHUB_CONFIRM_AS`, default

GitHub write, an MCP downstream's tool or `axhub.memory_delete` behaves like `vps.run`: held, pushed, run by Vinnie
unless denied. `allow` and `deny` are unchanged.

## 2. The answer to `call`

A `call` on a veto tool is **not rejected**. It is answered at once as an MCP tool result (not `isError`):

```json

  "held": true,
  "id": "6f1c2b9e-3d4a-4e7b-9a51-0c2d8e7f1a23",
  "jobId": "b0e4d1c2-7a8f-4c3d-9e21-5f6a7b8c9d0e",
  "runsAt": "2026-10-29T01:38:00.000Z",
  "secondsLeft": 180,
  "approvalUrl": "https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/6f1c2b9e-3d4a-4e7b-9a51-0c2d8e7f1a23",
  "denyUrl": "/auth/api/approvals/6f1c2b9e-3d4a-4e7b-9a51-0c2d8e7f1a23/deny",
  "streamUrl": "/auth/api/jobs/b0e4d1c2-7a8f-4c3d-9e21-5f6a7b8c9d0e/stream",
  "next_step": "Held on a 180 s veto countdown: … read it once later with get_job(\"b0e4…\")."
}
```

The caller reads the result later with `get_job(jobId)` (once; never poll). `hold: false` makes no difference to veto
tools. Ids are UUIDs (they match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}$`). `denyUrl` and `streamUrl` are relative to the hub.

## 3. States

```
held ──(countdown ends, ≤ 60 s late)──▶ running ──▶ ran | failed
  ├──(Deny)──▶ denied
  └──(hub was down past runsAt by > 60 s)──▶ expired   (logged; never run late)
```

| veto state | confirmation `status` | job `state` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `held` | `held` | `awaiting_confirmation` |
| `running` | `approved` → `consumed` (decidedBy `system:vinnie`) | `running` |
| `ran` | `consumed` | `succeeded` |
| `failed` (error, or exit code ≠ 0) | `consumed` | `succeeded` (exit ≠ 0, output kept) / `failed` / `cancelled` |
| `denied` | `rejected` | `cancelled` |
| `expired` | `expired` | `cancelled` |

Origin + `X-AxHub-CSRF` + JSON (the MCP bearer token never reaches it). Compare-and-set on status + revision, audited
(`denied veto <id> (<n> s left)`).

- `409 too_late` (countdown already ended, or already denied), `409 changed` (revision), `409 not_veto`, `404`.

```

10-second polling while something is held.

Output is what the connector returns anyway: redacted line by line (a private key block becomes one
`[redacted private key]` line), inside the 256 KB per-stream cap. A late watcher gets the current state, the output so
far (kept 15 minutes after the end) and `done`.

The AmberX app opens a terminal tab with the countdown when the timer starts and shows this stream in it.

| `running` | when the countdown ends and it starts |

`POST denyUrl`).

project/initialization/axhub-context.md:69:- **Policy engine:** per-service and per-tool `allow` / `confirm` / `deny`. Shell and destructive actions are default-deny. Since step 2: disabled services deny and are never contacted, SSH is denied unless a tool policy says otherwise, destructive tools are never below `confirm`, and evaluation is fail-closed (own-property lookups only, so tool names like `toString` can't slip through). A `confirm` call returns `confirmation_required` + id; **only the user approves it, out-of-band** (the operator CLI, or since decision #82 the approvals page `/auth/admin/approvals` for signed-in admins, phone first), never the AI client that asked. Since decision #101 the hub **keeps the call** (the MCP default) and runs it itself once approved, so Claude sends it once and never polls; the result is on a job the caller reads with `get_job` if it needs it (`hold: false` keeps the old retry-with-the-id flow). Since decision #103 (**veto everywhere**, server default `AXHUB_CONFIRM_AS=veto`) every call that would wait for an approval is held on the veto countdown instead and runs unless Brett denies it; approvals only come back with `AXHUB_CONFIRM_AS=confirm`. Since decision #102 a tool can also be **`veto`** (per tool; `vps.run` and `vps.logs`): the call is held on a countdown (default 180 s) and **Vinnie**, axHub's own agent, runs it by itself when the countdown ends unless the owner taps **Deny** first (no Approve; never more than 60 s late, else it expires); the approval page, the feeds and the console banner show the countdown, Vinnie pushes `held` / `warning` (30 s) / `running` through the ntfy topic the AmberX app delivers, and the job's output streams live at `/auth/api/jobs/<jobId>/stream` (contract `docs/veto.md`, veto@1). An approval shows the complete call (every argument, invisible characters escaped; calls with over 8000 characters of arguments can't be approved), the CLI asks y/N, and only the hub can issue approval requests. It is bound to the caller, the exact tool (including its definition) and arguments, single-use, and expires in 30 minutes. Since decision #95 the approvals page is a grid of every request (pending first; Approve on a collapsed row only when the row shows the complete call) with Approve, Decline, Postpone (a time or a condition from an open registry: time, service healthy, job done, public https URL answers), Ignore, Revoke and Reopen; a postponed request never runs, returns to pending (never approved) when its condition holds — checked every 5 minutes, reminders every 30 —, and can wait at most 7 days from when it was asked. Every change is compare-and-set on status + revision and audited. Since decision #96 these pages (and Users, Account, Apps, Handoff) are the AXHub web app on the hub's own address, calling the hub's session-only JSON API `/auth/api/*` (hub Origin + `X-AxHub-CSRF`, never the bearer token); the hub's old page addresses redirect there. Connectors receive the tool the hub checked, so a downstream that changes a tool can't run something else under its name (REST tools are signed with their exact request).

content.content:
# Approvals (veto) — AmberX plugin

Held commands (veto@1, Brett Oct 28 2026). Claude sends a command request to the VPS through Vinnie on axHub; the hub
holds it for a 3-minute countdown and then runs it itself unless Brett denies it. There is no Approve.

- **Notifications:** timer started (title, command, live countdown, **Deny**), time running out (30 s left), running.
  Android: the watch service (`android/.../VetoAlerts.java`), one channel per phase made with the chosen sound and
  vibration. Browser: this page while it is open (Notification API, tones, `navigator.vibrate`).
- **Settings → Plugins → Approvals:** timer-started sound, vibration, time-running-out sound, running sound, each with
  Test; "Open a terminal tab when a timer starts".
- **Terminal** (nav → Terminal): one tab per held command, with the countdown and Deny, then the live output from the
  hub's job stream and the final state (ran / failed / denied / expired).
- **Deny:** Android posts it with the phone's hub session (hub Origin + CSRF); a browser opens the call on the hub.

Contract and parsing: `framework/libs/hub/veto.ts`. Docs: `_claude/memory/docs/veto-approvals.md`.

Remove: `node framework/cli/plugin-catalog.mjs app-uninstall amberx approvals`. Outside this folder only the shell's
`VetoAlerts.java` and its seam in `src/native.ts` remain (shared shell code; inert without this plugin's settings).

## Assistant title bar (Oct 28 2026)

This plugin also plugs the phone's deciding path into lib-approvals (`framework/libs/approvals`), whose badge sits in
the assistant's title bar (the AI plugin's Ask view, and the console AI assistant's chat when it runs here):
`setApprovalsHost({ hub, frame: false, decide: decideFromPhone })` in `register`. Deny = native `vetoDeny` (fallback:
the call's page); Approve / Decline open the approval in the signed-in hub web view. A tapped approval notification
dispatches `approvals.popover:<id>` (the monitor's `open` listener) and the popover opens on that item.
12:- **Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103):** every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
33:- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
39:- **It's a veto system, not approvals (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "It's not an approval system anymore. It's a veto system. … You send the notice that you're going to be making changes, and then my VPS waits three minutes before sending it unless I click deny … you don't stop, you just build and you don't check for its completion."; axHub decision #103):** every axHub call that needs Brett (VPS commands, GitHub writes, PRs, merges, deletes on the hub, any MCP tool) is a **veto call**: axHub holds it, pushes the notice through the AmberX app, and Vinnie runs it after the 3-minute countdown unless he taps **Deny**. Send it **once** with its `reason`, tell Brett in one line what is coming (the Deny link is optional, never "approve"), and **keep building**: don't wait for the countdown, don't poll, don't re-send, don't schedule checks for its completion, don't ask him to approve anything. Read the job with `get_job` only when a later step truly needs its output, and only once. A denied call stays denied unless he asks again. (Replaces "Send approvals once, never poll" #101, "Approvals" Oct 20 with its retry timing, and "Veto calls are sent once" Oct 28.)
40:- **Automatic merge (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "When stuff needs to merge automatic merge"; replaces "Ready to merge = send him a merge approval", Oct 27):** PRs merge by themselves. The console's push banner auto-merges every open PR in the watched repos (AmberX-AXF, axHub, Build-Pilot by default) that is ready: not a draft, no conflicts, CI passed on its head commit (pinned) — every 3 minutes, no Claude session, no tokens (setting *Auto-merge* in Settings → Plugins → Push banner, on by default). So a session just opens the PR (`github.pulls/create` or the push banner's Open PR, a veto call) and moves on: no merge call, no asking, no checking. A repo without CI never gets a green result and never auto-merges, so every watched repo has CI (axHub: `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `pnpm test`, since Oct 30 2026). <!-- axf-plugin:push-banner -->
42:- **Deny is on the first screen (Oct 27 2026, Brett; veto since Oct 30 2026):** every notice and AXHub page for a held call shows the countdown and **Deny** on the first screen, right under the title, before the description and the code. Keep `reason.title` one short line so it stays there on a phone.
48:- **Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett):** anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's **systems check banner** as an item with **Auto fix**, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.

# Veto approvals (veto@1), AmberX-AXF side

Brett, Oct 28 2026 21:35 EDT: "Change approval system: Claude sends a command request to the VPS through Vinnie on
axHub. Vinnie sends a notification through the AmberX Android app that waits 3 minutes before running the command in
the AmberX terminal through Vinnie. After the 3-minute countdown appears on the approval page and in a banner in the
console — but instead of an Approve button I can Deny it and stop it from running before time is up. Put a setting in
AmberX to configure the notification sound and vibration, and the notification sound for time running out and for
running. When the timer starts, open a tab in the AmberX terminal with the countdown before running."

Built on branch `refactor-all/veto` (refactor-all steps s83–s86, group veto-approvals, Opus). The hub side (axHub repo,
branch `claude/veto-approvals`) holds, counts down, runs and streams the call; this repo shows it and lets Brett deny it.

## The contract this side reads (veto@1)

- Feed `GET /auth/api/approvals` and legacy `/auth/admin/approvals.json`: a held call is in `pending` with
  `status: "held"`, `veto: { runsAt, secondsLeft, countdownSeconds }`, `jobId`, `denyUrl`, `streamUrl`; also in `held[]`
  with `heldCount`. The explain layer (`/auth/api/approvals/<id>`) carries `status: "held"` + the same `veto`.
- Deny: `POST /auth/api/approvals/<id>/deny` (admin session + hub Origin + `X-AxHub-CSRF`).
- Stream: `GET /auth/api/jobs/<jobId>/stream` (SSE `countdown {secondsLeft}`, `state {state}`, `output {stream, text}`,
  `done {state, exitCode}`).
- Push: `{ type: "veto", phase: "held"|"warning"|"running", id, jobId, title, command, runsAt, secondsLeft, denyUrl,
  streamUrl, approvalUrl }`.
- States: held → running → ran | failed; denied; expired.

## What was built, where

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Parser + client (web) | `framework/libs/hub/veto.ts` (baked into amberx-droid, console-web, axhub-web `src/axf/libs/hub/veto.ts`): `interpretVeto`, `splitFeed`, `fetchVetoFeed` (same read rules as `fetchHubFeed`), `secondsLeftNow` (local clock), `vetoPhase` (30 s warning), `notifyPlan`, `vetoFromPush`, `vetoEvent` + `followVeto` (SSE), `denyVeto` (hub-origin pages). `hub.ts` is unchanged. Kotlin twin deferred (PORTING.md). |
| AmberX notifications (s83) | Plugin `apps/amberx-droid/src/plugins/approvals` (store, settings, browser notifications + tones). Shell: `android/.../VetoAlerts.java` (one channel per phase made from the chosen sound + vibration; one card per call with a live countdown and a **Deny** action; warning and running scheduled at their local times; Deny posted with the phone's hub session), `HubRules.vetoes` / `deny`, `WatchService.check` (reads every 10 s while something is held), `native.ts` `vetoSettings` / `vetoDeny` / `vetoTest` + `veto` events. Held calls are never shown as approvals and never auto-approved on the phone. |
| AmberX settings | Settings → Plugins → **Approvals**: timer-started sound, vibration, time-running-out sound, running sound (Android: notification default / alarm / ringtone / silent; browser: tones), each with **Test**; "Open a terminal tab when a timer starts". |
| AmberX Terminal (s84) | `plugins/approvals/web/terminal.tsx`, nav → **Terminal**, action `approvals.terminal[:<id>]`: a tab per held call with title, command, countdown, Deny; output from the job stream when it runs; final state kept until closed. The console's Terminal plugin is a PTY on the console server, so it isn't installed in AmberX. |
| Console banner (s85) | `apps/console-web/plugins/approvals-banner` 0.3.0: held rows with countdown + Deny (no Review/Approve); Deny/tap opens the call's page on the hub in the review dialog. |
| AXHub web app (s85) | `apps/axhub-web/src/views/HeldCall.tsx`: countdown + Deny on the first screen of `ApprovalDetail` (in place of the actions; re-reads every 3 s) and in the grid row's header; no Approve. |
| Rule (s86) | `_claude/shared/rules/RULES.md`: "Veto calls are sent once and never polled". |

## How to test

- `npx -y tsx apps/amberx-droid/test.mjs` (veto block: feed split, links, countdown, notify plan, push, stream, deny, alert config, store).
- `cd apps/amberx-droid && npm run build`; `cd apps/axhub-web && npm run build`; `cd apps/console-web && npm run typecheck && npm run build`.
- `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-controls.mjs`.
- Android (CI): `HubRulesTest.heldVetoCalls`; on the phone: Settings → Plugins → Approvals → each Test button plays its
  channel; send a held `vps.run` through axHub and check the three notifications, Deny from the notification, and the
  Terminal tab.
- Browser: open AmberX, allow notifications, Test buttons play tones; a held call opens a Terminal tab.

## Known gaps

- AmberX has no push transport yet (the phone polls the feed); `vetoFromPush` is ready for it.
- AmberX's own Approvals page, the monitor's in-browser alerts and lib-hub `fetchHubFeed` still count a held call as
  waiting (hub.ts unchanged; filtering there is a cross-port contract change).
- Deny from the console or a browser opens the hub page (the hub accepts a Deny only under its own Origin).
52 _claude/memory/docs/veto-approvals.md

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# axhub — run the axHub operator CLI inside the live Coolify container.
# Usage: axhub <command> ...   (same commands as the CLI, e.g. `axhub vault set github-token`)
# Finds the current container by its Coolify app id, so it survives redeploys.
set -euo pipefail
APP_ID="${AXHUB_COOLIFY_APP:-jghxpzuudkahgznvffiwtwmj}"
C=$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep "^${APP_ID}" | head -1 || true)
if [ -z "$C" ]; then
  echo "axhub: no running container whose name starts with ${APP_ID}" >&2
  exit 1
fi
TTY=()
if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY=(-t); fi
exec docker exec -i "${TTY[@]}" "$C" axhub "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# merge-pr.sh <owner/repo> <number> — merge a pull request through the Dev Console's push banner (Brett, Oct 27 2026:
# "When something is ready for merge send approval message to merge"). Sessions run it through axHub `vps.run`, so
# every merge waits for Brett's approval on axHub; it never runs from cron or by itself.
#
# The push banner's POST /merge only merges an open, non-draft PR GitHub can merge, whose CI on the head commit passed,
# with that commit pinned (never a direct push to main). The console token is read inside the console container from
# its env file, so no token is ever in a command, a log or an approval page.
set -euo pipefail
REPO="${1:?usage: merge-pr.sh <owner/repo> <number>}"
NUM="${2:?usage: merge-pr.sh <owner/repo> <number>}"
[[ "$REPO" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || { echo "not a repo name: $REPO" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ "$NUM" =~ ^[0-9]{1,7}$ ]] || { echo "not a PR number: $NUM" >&2; exit 2; }
CONTAINER="${AXF_CONSOLE_CONTAINER:-axf-console}"
docker exec -i -e MERGE_REPO="$REPO" -e MERGE_NUM="$NUM" "$CONTAINER" python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os, re, sys, urllib.error, urllib.request
repo, num = os.environ["MERGE_REPO"], int(os.environ["MERGE_NUM"])
env = open("/axf/.axf-console/env", encoding="utf-8").read()
m = re.search(r"^AXF_TOKEN=(.+)$", env, re.M)
if not m:
    sys.exit("no console token in /axf/.axf-console/env")
port = os.environ.get("PORT", "7090")
req = urllib.request.Request(
    f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/plugins/push-banner/merge",
    json.dumps({"repo": repo, "number": num, "confirm": f"{repo}#{num}"}).encode(),
    {"Authorization": "Bearer " + m.group(1).strip(), "Content-Type": "application/json"},
)
try:
    print(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60).read().decode())
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    print(f"refused ({e.code}): {e.read().decode(errors='replace')[:600]}")
    sys.exit(1)
PY

content.text:
The veto system is finished and both branches are pushed. Nothing is merged. A veto call to open the two PRs (AXF and axHub, branch `claude/veto-complete`) went out at 18:16 UTC with a 90 s countdown. Deny it here if you don't want them opened: https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/f2a1a0f9-161c-42c5-9315-579314ea4c97. Under the auto-merge rule they merge by themselves only once CI is green.

**What changed**
- **90 s countdown:** this is now the hub's default. I've already set the live `vps.run` and `vps.logs` to 90 s. GitHub, Hostinger and other MCP calls get 90 s once the axHub PR is deployed.
- **Approve and Shelve next to Deny (axHub decision #104):**
  - **Approve** runs the call within a second and sends no more notices.
  - **Shelve** pauses the countdown until you approve or deny. A shelved call left alone for 7 days expires without running.
  - Both have the same safety checks as Deny, plus CLI commands. The AI client can never approve, hurry or shelve a call.
- **The approvals banner plugin is now the veto banner:**
  - It owns the veto screen (countdown plus Deny / Approve / Shelve), the notices and the alarm.
  - It runs in the console and in AmberX.
  - **Alarm settings:** on/off, tone (built-in or your own sound file), volume, louder over time, ring length, repeats and gap, vibration, when it starts, and ring through silent mode. There are Test and Stop buttons.
- **AmberX phone:**
  - Notices carry Deny / Approve / Shelve buttons.
  - Tapping a notice opens the veto screen.
  - A small native part plays the alarm on the alarm channel, so it rings when the phone is on silent.
  - AmberX's own approvals plugin is now just the Terminal view. Its old sound settings are gone because the alarm replaces them.
- **axHub approval page:** shows Approve and Shelve next to Deny.
